title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 26 Sep to 20 Oct 2026
summary: Between 26 Sep and 20 Oct 2026 the whole circle around Beni Mellal got brighter, with mean HH up 1.11 dB and 8.03 km2 brighter in HH. The 20 Oct date carries a flag, so most of this brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 24 days mean HV rose by 0.63 dB. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 8.03 km2 and darker on only 0.29 km2. In HV, 3.73 km2 turned brighter and 0.37 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 3.67 km2 brighter in HH and rose 1.58 dB, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 1.67 km2 brighter. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 1.11 dB in HH. The changing fields had 0.83 km2 brighter in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 20 Oct product, since the city brightened like the fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain, which raises the echo from soil and walls; rain records for October would check it. Possible cause for part of the field change: new crops; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 20 Oct 2026 carries a flag: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. It lowers confidence in every number from that date. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged date for any field or city figure, check rain records for October, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
